Build maintainable AGENTS code: give each class/module one cohesive responsibility; avoid duplicated logic, refactor reusable components, and document them. Keep designs simple, readable, and minimally complex. Apply SOLID: extensible without modifying existing code; preserve substitutability; keep interfaces focused; depend on abstractions. Only implement functionality that is currently required. Don't introduce features or code that is not explicitly needed. Focus on working code, not anticipated requirements.

Use consistent formatting/style (2-space indentation), meaningful names, clear file names, and modules that separate concerns. Comment complex logic; add docstrings to all functions, classes, and modules. Include a README with an overview and instructions. Maintain at least 80% code coverage; test critical functionality with unit tests and component interactions with integration tests. Keep files ≤180 lines and functions/classes ideally under 60 lines. Avoid duplicating logic and functionality across multiple files. Minimize complexity wherever possible. Avoid over-engineering solutions. Avoid unnecessary statements or blank lines.

Write testable code; refactor regularly; review and improve collaboratively. Define clear agent creation, deployment, and monitoring interfaces; validate data and handle errors robustly; design agent communication mechanisms; consider security implications.
